locator.text: Every JSON document a verifier reads MUST satisfy the following rules when it is loaded: each JSON member of a bundle (`manifest.json`, `p1.json`, `canonical_input.json`, the envelope and `verification_receipt.json`) and each document the caller supplies (the registry entry, the trust registry and the trust-root document).
Conforming implementations MUST reject violating documents before canonicalization; silent repair (for example last-wins duplicate resolution or precision-lossy number coercion) is non-conforming.
A JSON object MUST NOT contain two members with the same name after escape decoding (`"a"` and `"\u0061"` are the same name).

Every string, and every member name, MUST consist solely of Unicode scalar values: an unpaired surrogate (a code point in `U+D800` to `U+DFFF` that is not part of a valid pair) is invalid at parse time.
An implementation whose regular-expression engine lets `$` also match before a final newline (Python's `re` is the common case) MUST NOT accept a value carrying that trailing newline.

Every string, and every member name, MUST NOT contain a Unicode noncharacter: U+FDD0 to U+FDEF, and each code point whose last four hexadecimal digits are FFFE or FFFF (66 code points in all), whether it is written as the character itself or as an escape (`\uFDD0`, `\uFFFF`, or the pair `\uD83F\uDFFE` for U+1FFFE).

A file of the archive outside the selected root was delivered beside the bundle and is committed to by nothing: a verifier **MUST** report it, and the run yields `OFFLINE_REVIEW`, as for an undeclared member.
Every other file present in the bundle **MUST** be declared in `manifest.files` (the canonical input, `p1.json` and the `p1.sha256` sidecar included).

A bundle that carries a member at a reserved name, declared in `manifest.files` or not, is not refused for it and does not pass silently: a verifier **MUST** report it, and the run yields `OFFLINE_REVIEW` with the review reason `bundle_reserved_member` ([`report-contract.md`](report-contract.md) §3).
An undeclared member is not a silent pass: a verifier **MUST** report it, and the run yields `OFFLINE_REVIEW` rather than `OFFLINE_OK`.

When the host fails a listing of the inventory below the root, or the inspection of an entry of a listing, the run reports `bundle_inventory_failed`, a host failure; when any listing is refused by its names, it reports `bundle_member_name_invalid`; in neither case does it report `unsafe_bundle_member`, even for a link the verifier met before the failed or refused listing: which entries a verifier meets before it reaches that listing depends on the order in which it lists directories, which this specification does not fix, and a report **MUST NOT** depend on that order.
